intervention_label: HA-1 TCR-T (donor-derived CD8+/CD4+ memory T cells, Bleakley/HighPassBio platform)
intervention_dose: One or more infusions of HA-1 TCR-T after fludarabine/cyclophosphamide lymphodepletion; dose levels 3x10^6 to 1x10^7 TCR-T/kg
indication: Persistent or recurrent leukemia / myeloid neoplasm after allogeneic HCT
population_detail: 9 allo-HCT recipients with disease recurrence after transplant, recipient HA-1(H)-positive and HLA-A*02:01-positive with an HA-1-disparate donor. Prior allo-HCT is an entry requirement rather than an exclusion.
outcome: Complete remission achieved or maintained after lymphodepletion + HA-1 TCR-T
median_dor_or_pfs: One patient in continuing remission beyond 2 years; one MRD-negative for >27 months

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: 4/9 achieved or maintained CR; trial not powered for efficacy

outcomes.name: AE_rate
outcomes.notes: no dose-limiting toxicity, no CRS, no ICANS

safety_summary: No dose-limiting toxicity, no CRS and no ICANS across 9 infused patients. Grade 3-4 neutropenia and grade 3-5 infections followed the lymphodepletion; two cases of mild acute GVHD were attributed to immunosuppression withdrawal before infusion rather than to the product.

toxicities.notes: attributed to immunosuppression withdrawal, not to TCR-T
grade 3-4 in multiple patients, lymphodepletion-attributed; per-patient counts not tabulated

notes: The only HA-1 programme whose protocol requires prior allo-HCT, which is why it survives the eligibility screen where TSC-100/101 and BSB-1001 do not. Safety data read from the PMC full text (PMC11406181); the paper reports events narratively rather than in a per-term grade table.

intervention_label: HA-1 / HA-2 minor-histocompatibility-antigen TCR-T (class review, incl. TSC-100/TSC-101)
exclusion_reason: Narrative review without extractable primary effect estimates; the TSC-100/TSC-101 (ALLOHA) results it summarises remain conference-abstract level, and that protocol excludes prior allo-HCT so this patient could not enrol regardless.
notes: Read to check whether any peer-reviewed TSC-100/101 efficacy numbers exist. They do not; the review cites early-phase safety and persistence in general terms.

intervention_label: WT1-TCRC4 CD8+ T cells (TTCR-C4, HLA-A*02:01-restricted), prophylactic post-HCT
intervention_dose: EBV-specific donor CD8+ T cells transduced with TCRC4, infused prophylactically after allo-HCT
indication: High-risk AML in remission after allogeneic HCT
population_detail: 12 HLA-A2-positive patients transplanted for poor-risk AML and infused while in remission; contemporaneous comparison group of 88 similar-risk AML patients from the same programme.
design: Phase 1/2 single-arm with contemporaneous non-randomised comparison group (NCT01640301)
comparator: Concurrent comparative group of 88 similar-risk AML patients
median_dor_or_pfs: 100% relapse-free at a median of 44 months after infusion

outcomes.name: AE_rate
outcomes.notes: no grade 3+ event attributed to the product

safety_summary: No CRS and no pulmonary toxicity; no grade 3+ event was attributed to the infusions. One grade 3 acute GVHD occurred 97 days after infusion and was judged unrelated on timing and tissue-localisation grounds. Chronic GVHD was 55% in treated patients versus 61% in the comparison group.
notes: Prophylactic infusion into patients in remission. Read against Mazziotta 2025, which applied the same product to active post-HCT disease and did not reproduce the benefit; that is the population this patient sits in.

intervention_label: WT1-TCRC4 CD8+ T cells (TTCR-C4, HLA-A*02:01-restricted), active disease post-HCT
intervention_dose: EBV- or CMV-specific donor CD8+ T cells transduced with TCRC4; one or more infusions post-HCT
indication: Relapsed and/or refractory AML after allogeneic HCT
population_detail: 15 HLA-A2-positive patients with relapsed/refractory AML post-HCT enrolled 2013-2019. At infusion two had overt disease, five were MRD-positive, and the rest had no evaluable disease.
median_dor_or_pfs: Median OS 242 days

outcomes.name: RR
outcomes.notes: 4/15 without overt relapse and/or MRD after infusion

safety_summary: Infusions were safe and well tolerated with no dose-limiting toxicity and no product-related serious adverse event. One patient (about 7%) developed grade 3 acute GVHD and one moderate chronic GVHD after infusion.
notes: The negative counterpart to Chapuis 2019: in active post-HCT disease the same TCR did not improve outcomes over historical controls, with the transferred cells skewing to an NK-like terminally differentiated state. Safety detail from PMC12141728.

intervention_dose: Two infusions 4 weeks apart in a dose-escalating design, followed by sequential WT1 peptide vaccination
indication: Refractory AML and high-risk MDS
population_detail: 8 HLA-A*24:02-positive patients with refractory AML or high-risk MDS across two dose cohorts. Restriction is A*24:02, so this route stays open if A*02:01 typing returns negative.
median_dor_or_pfs: 4 of the 5 patients with persisting T cells at study end survived beyond 12 months

outcomes.name: RR
outcomes.notes: 2/8 with transient marrow blast decrease and haematopoietic recovery; no formal CR

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: 5/8 with TCR-T persisting throughout the study period

safety_summary: No adverse events involving normal tissue were seen across both dose cohorts; the report describes no on-target off-tumour toxicity.
notes: Activity signal is a transient blast reduction in 2 of 8, not remission. Its value here is the alternative HLA restriction: it is the one WT1 handle that does not require A*02:01. No per-term AE table is published beyond the statement that normal-tissue events did not occur.

intervention_dose: 0.1 to 5 x 10^6 TCR-T cells/kg after lymphodepleting chemotherapy
indication: Relapsed/refractory AML, MDS and multiple myeloma
population_detail: 13 HLA-A*02:01-positive patients enrolled, 9 infused. Advanced disease stage and rapid progression in the R/R AML subset limited what could be read out.

outcomes.name: RR
outcomes.notes: measurable clinical response in 2 of 9 infused

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: PRAME mRNA reduction in marrow or blood in 7 of 9

safety_summary: No dose-limiting toxicities. Serious adverse events were mostly attributable to lymphodepleting chemotherapy or disease progression; CRS occurred in two patients.
notes: Medigene stopped the programme after phase 1. The authors' own reading is that tumour burden was the limiting factor, which matters for a patient at 85% marrow blasts.

intervention_label: Donor-derived multi-leukemia-antigen-specific T cells (mLSTs targeting PRAME, WT1, survivin, NY-ESO-1)
intervention_dose: 0.5 to 10 x 10^7 cells/m2 in an escalating design
indication: AML/MDS after allogeneic HCT, high relapse risk or overt relapse
population_detail: 25 patients infused, 17 at high risk of relapse and 8 with relapsed disease. Products were generated from 29 HCT donors and were not HLA-restricted to a single allele.
outcome: Objective response in the active-disease cohort
median_dor_or_pfs: Median leukemia-free and overall survival not reached at 1.9 years of follow-up

outcomes.name: PFS
outcomes.notes: leukemia-free survival at 1.9 years median follow-up

safety_summary: Infusions were well tolerated with no acute GVHD above grade 2 and no extensive chronic GVHD.
notes: This is the ADSPAM protocol whose Group B admits post-transplant relapse and counts extramedullary sites as qualifying disease, which is why the thigh sarcoma does not disqualify. Response numbers in the active-disease arm are 2 of 8.

intervention_dose: 12 microg/kg IV on days 1-5 of each 21-day cycle
indication: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm, untreated or relapsed
population_detail: 47 patients assigned across 7 and 12 microg/kg cohorts; the primary-outcome population was the 29 previously untreated patients dosed at 12 microg/kg. Median age 70.
outcome: Complete response or clinical complete response
median_dor_or_pfs: Survival 59% at 18 months and 52% at 24 months
safety_summary: Capillary leak syndrome occurred in 19% of the 47 treated patients and caused one death in each dose subgroup. Transaminase elevation, hypoalbuminaemia, peripheral oedema and thrombocytopenia were the common events.

toxicities.notes: one fatal case in each dose subgroup

notes: Registration trial for the only approved CD123-directed agent, in BPDCN rather than AML. It is the reason tagraxofusp exists as an off-label CD123 option and nothing more; the 72% figure does not transfer to AML.

intervention_dose: Tagraxofusp 12 microg/kg days 1-3, azacitidine 75 mg/m2 for 7 days, venetoclax for 21 days (recommended phase 2 schedule)
indication: CD123-positive AML and high-risk MDS
population_detail: 56 adults enrolled; the untreated-AML triplet expansion was 26 patients, median age 71, all ELN adverse-risk, half TP53-mutated. 13 of the 26 carried a TP53 mutation.
outcome: Overall response (CR + CRi + MLFS) in untreated AML
median_dor_or_pfs: Median OS 14 months, median PFS 8.5 months
safety_summary: Capillary leak syndrome was 18.9% with the triplet versus 47% with the tagraxofusp-azacitidine doublet. Grade 3+ cytopenias dominated: thrombocytopenia 45.9%, low white count 45.9%, neutropenia 37.8%. 30-day mortality was 10.8% on the triplet with one treatment-related death from multiorgan failure.
notes: Closest CD123 evidence to this case because half the cohort was TP53-mutated and all were ELN adverse-risk, but the population is untreated AML rather than post-transplant refractory disease. Safety extracted from PMC10837492.

exclusion_reason: BPDCN-only phase 2; the AML-relevant tagraxofusp combination evidence from the same NCT03113643 programme is already captured in Lane 2024 Blood Advances.
notes: Read for the transplant-bridging signal (63% of the frontline cohort reached allo-HCT), which supports the sequencing logic but adds no AML effect estimate.

intervention_dose: 0.045 mg/kg IV once every 3 weeks (recommended phase 2 dose)
indication: Relapsed or refractory CD123-positive AML
population_detail: 91 enrolled overall (68 on the every-3-week schedule A); the efficacy estimate below is the 29 patients treated at the recommended phase 2 dose. ECOG 0-1 required.
design: First-in-human phase 1/2, dose escalation and expansion (NCT03386513)
outcome: Overall response rate at the recommended phase 2 dose
safety_summary: At the recommended phase 2 dose the commonest grade 3+ treatment-related events were febrile neutropenia 10%, infusion-related reactions 7% and anaemia 7%. Three dose-limiting toxicities occurred across escalation, two of them reversible veno-occlusive disease; one death on schedule A was considered treatment-related.
notes: The single-agent activity estimate the board will want when weighing a CD123 ADC against cellular options. Veno-occlusive disease in a patient heading toward a second transplant is the specific risk to weigh.

intervention_label: Pivekimab sunirine (CD123 ADC) in BPDCN — approval-supporting data
intervention_dose: 0.045 mg/kg IV once every 3 weeks
indication: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm, frontline and relapsed/refractory
population_detail: 84 patients: 33 frontline (22 de novo, 20 forming the primary analysis population) and 51 relapsed/refractory. Median age 72.
outcome: Composite complete response rate in frontline de novo BPDCN
median_dor_or_pfs: Median duration of composite CR 10.6 months frontline, 9.2 months relapsed/refractory

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.subgroup: frontline de novo primary analysis population

safety_summary: Peripheral oedema 54%, fatigue 26% and infusion-related reactions 26% were the commonest events. Grade 3+ events were neutropenia 16%, thrombocytopenia 14% and peripheral oedema 12%; serious events included pneumonia 6%.

toxicities.notes: reported as a serious adverse event

notes: The dataset behind the May 2026 FDA approval, which is in BPDCN and not AML. Relevant here only as evidence that the CD123 ADC is now commercially available and therefore reachable off-label or by expanded access.

intervention_dose: 500 ng/kg/day continuous infusion (recommended phase 2 dose), with step-up dosing in week 1 and pretreatment dexamethasone
indication: Relapsed/refractory AML, primary induction failure or early relapse
population_detail: 88 adults with R/R AML overall (42 dose-finding, 46 at the recommended phase 2 dose). The efficacy estimate is the 30 primary-induction-failure or early-relapse patients treated at the recommended dose.
outcome: CR / CR with partial haematological recovery in primary induction failure or early relapse
median_dor_or_pfs: Median OS 10.2 months among those achieving CR/CRh
safety_summary: Infusion-related reactions and CRS were near-universal at 96% any grade in the expansion population but only 8% reached grade 3, with no grade 4-5 events. Grade 3+ cytopenias were the next most common. No treatment-related deaths.
notes: MacroGenics terminated the programme for business reasons in 2022, so the drug is not obtainable. It stays in the dossier because 26.7% CR/CRh in exactly the chemorefractory population this patient occupies is the best CD123 x CD3 benchmark on record. Safety from PMC7885824.

intervention_dose: 500 ng/kg/day continuous infusion
indication: Relapsed/refractory AML with TP53 mutation and/or 17p deletion
population_detail: 15 of 45 flotetuzumab-treated patients with marrow transcriptomic profiling carried TP53 mutations and/or 17p deletion. Responders had higher baseline tumour-inflammation, FOXP3, CD8 and PD1 signature scores.
design: Correlative analysis nested in the phase 1/2 trial (NCT02152956)
outcome: Complete response (<5% marrow blasts) in TP53-abnormal R/R AML
median_dor_or_pfs: Median OS 10.3 months among TP53-abnormal complete responders (range 3.3-21.3)
notes: Post-hoc biomarker analysis on 15 patients, so the 47% carries wide uncertainty the paper does not quantify. Checked the PubMed abstract and the PMC full text (PMC7594389): this correlative paper carries no safety section, so toxicities[] is empty and the parent-trial toxicity sits on the Uy 2021 row.

intervention_dose: Weekly IV with step-up; optimised target dose at least 0.75 microg/kg
indication: Relapsed/refractory AML
population_detail: 120 patients dosed, 111 AML patients evaluable for response; 87 evaluable at the optimised dose of at least 0.75 microg/kg.
safety_summary: CRS in 85% of 120 patients, grade 3+ in 27 patients with one grade 5 event. 87.5% had at least one grade 3+ treatment-emergent event; anaemia, febrile neutropenia and pneumonia led. Eight deaths from treatment-emergent events, one attributed directly to vibecotamab.
notes: The second CD123 x CD3 readout and a considerably weaker one than flotetuzumab: 9% response with 27% grade 3+ CRS. Safety from PMC10632668.

intervention_dose: Lintuzumab-Ac225 0.25-1.0 microCi/kg given 7 (+2) days after CLAG-M days 1-6; RP2D 0.75 microCi/kg
indication: Relapsed/refractory AML
population_detail: 26 patients (21 in 3+3 escalation, 5 at the RP2D); 86.7% of evaluable patients had high-risk disease. Separate readouts for TP53-mutated and prior-venetoclax subgroups.
median_dor_or_pfs: Estimated 1-year PFS 30.8% (95% CI 14.6-48.5)
safety_summary: Grade 3/4 febrile neutropenia 65.4% and decreased white cells 50%; the authors describe the profile as expected for CLAG-M plus an alpha-emitting radioconjugate.
notes: The most directly transferable CD33 datapoint in this set: R/R AML, high-risk disease, and separate 50% TP53-mutated and 38.5% prior-venetoclax subgroup rates. Abstract-level safety only; no per-term grade table beyond the two events listed.

intervention_dose: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin 3 mg/m2 on days 1, 4 and 7, one course
indication: AML in first relapse
population_detail: 57 patients in first relapse. Remission correlated with P-glycoprotein and MRP1 activity, which is the drug-efflux axis rather than CD33 density.
median_dor_or_pfs: Median relapse-free survival 11 months
safety_summary: Median neutropenia below 500/microL lasted 23 days and thrombocytopenia below 50,000/microL 21 days. No grade 3-4 liver toxicity and no veno-occlusive disease, including in the seven patients transplanted afterwards.
notes: The origin of fractionated dosing and the reason gemtuzumab can precede a transplant without veno-occlusive disease. First relapse after chemotherapy, not refractory disease after allo-HCT, so the 26% is an upper bound here.

intervention_label: Fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin added to daunorubicin/cytarabine (ALFA-0701)
intervention_dose: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin 3 mg/m2 on days 1, 4 and 7 of induction and day 1 of each consolidation course
indication: Untreated de novo AML, age 50-70
population_detail: 280 randomised, 139 analysed per arm. De novo AML only; secondary and treatment-related AML were not enrolled.
median_dor_or_pfs: 2-year EFS 40.8% with gemtuzumab versus 17.1% without
safety_summary: Persistent thrombocytopenia was the differentiating toxicity, 16% with gemtuzumab versus 3% without (p<0.0001), with no increase in death from toxicity.
notes: The randomised basis for fractionated gemtuzumab and the reason CD33 counts as an actionable handle. Untreated de novo AML in a fitter age band, so it establishes the mechanism rather than the expected benefit here.

intervention_label: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin added to induction — individual-patient-data meta-analysis
intervention_dose: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin with first-course induction; 3 mg/m2 and 6 mg/m2 dose levels compared
indication: Adult AML (excluding acute promyelocytic leukaemia)
population_detail: 3325 patients across five randomised trials, with a prespecified exploratory stratification by cytogenetic risk group.
design: Individual-patient-data meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
outcome: Six-year absolute survival benefit by cytogenetic risk
safety_summary: Doses of 3 mg/m2 produced fewer early deaths than 6 mg/m2 with equal efficacy, which is the basis of the fractionated schedule.

toxicities.notes: fewer at 3 mg/m2 than 6 mg/m2 with equal efficacy; per-arm counts not given in the abstract

notes: Carries the caveat the board most needs on CD33: patients with adverse cytogenetics showed no survival benefit (OR 0.99, 0.83-1.18, p=0.9). This patient's karyotype is complex and adverse.

intervention_dose: 1.12 x 10^9 autologous T cells, approximately 38% CAR-transduced, single infusion
indication: Refractory AML
population_detail: Single 41-year-old male patient with refractory AML and pre-existing pancytopenia.
design: Single-patient report from a phase 1 trial (NCT01864902)
effect_size: marked decrease at 2 weeks, progression by 9 weeks
median_dor_or_pfs: Disease progression at 9 weeks after infusion

outcomes.name: other
outcomes.effect_size: marked marrow blast decrease at 2 weeks
outcomes.notes: gradual rise thereafter with florid progression at 9 weeks

safety_summary: The infusion alone produced rigorous chills and fever, sharp swings in pre-existing pancytopenia, raised IL-6, IL-8, TNF-alpha and interferon-gamma, and transient mild hyperbilirubinaemia within 2 weeks.
notes: A single patient is the whole published clinical experience for CD33 CAR-T in adults. Anything the board says about NCT05672147 rests on this plus preclinical work.

exclusion_reason: Preclinical only — in vitro and xenograft construct comparison, no patients treated.
notes: Read to see whether any clinical CD33 CAR-T efficacy exists beyond the 2015 single-patient report. It does not; this paper is the preclinical basis for the current phase 1.

intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, high-dose cytarabine, gemtuzumab ozogamicin) frontline in core-binding-factor AML
exclusion_reason: Wrong population and line — frontline core-binding-factor AML in fit patients, which is the favourable-cytogenetics group where gemtuzumab benefit is concentrated. This patient has complex adverse karyotype and refractory disease.
notes: Read while looking for any published CLAG-GO efficacy. NCT04050280, the R/R CLAG-GO phase 2 that fits this case, is still recruiting with no results posted, so the regimen currently has no direct evidence in refractory AML.

intervention_dose: Eprenetapopt 4.5 g/day IV days 1-4, venetoclax 400 mg/day days 1-28, azacitidine 75 mg/m2 days 1-7, 28-day cycles
indication: TP53-mutated AML, treatment-naive
population_detail: 49 enrolled across cohorts; the response estimate is the 39 patients on the triplet. At least one pathogenic TP53 mutation was required, ECOG 0-2, median age 67.
safety_summary: Grade 3+ events in at least 20%: febrile neutropenia 47%, thrombocytopenia 37%, leukopenia 25%, anaemia 22%. Treatment-related serious events in 27% and one treatment-related death from sepsis.
notes: Treatment-naive AML, not relapsed disease, and the parallel randomised phase 3 of eprenetapopt plus azacitidine in TP53-mutant MDS missed its endpoint, after which the programme stopped. The 38% belongs to a population and a development path that no longer apply.

intervention_dose: Eprenetapopt 3.7 g/day IV days 1-4 and azacitidine 36 mg/m2 days 1-5, 28-day cycles, up to 12 cycles
indication: TP53-mutated AML and MDS after allogeneic HCT
population_detail: 33 of 55 transplanted patients started maintenance (14 AML, 19 MDS), median age 65. Screening began before transplant, so the cohort is enriched for patients who reached and tolerated HCT.
median_dor_or_pfs: Median RFS 12.5 months; median OS 20.6 months
safety_summary: 30-day mortality from first dose was 0% and 60-day mortality 6% (2 patients). All-grade acute GVHD occurred in 12% and chronic GVHD in 33%.
notes: The one eprenetapopt setting that maps onto this case's shape — TP53-mutant myeloid disease consolidated after allo-HCT — but it is single-arm with heavy selection: only 33 of 84 screened reached maintenance.

exclusion_reason: Trial-protocol paper with no efficacy results; PYNNACLE enrols solid tumours requiring RECIST-measurable disease, so a marrow-based leukaemia cannot contribute. Interim response rates circulating for this drug come from sponsor press releases rather than peer-reviewed publication.
notes: Read to establish whether any peer-reviewed rezatapopt effect size exists. None does. NCT06616636, the AML/MDS trial, has only just opened.

intervention_label: Rezatapopt in TP53-Y220C AML — mechanism study
exclusion_reason: Preclinical (cell lines, primary samples, xenografts); no patients treated.
notes: Kept in the audit trail because it tempers the Y220C hypothesis: rezatapopt restored wild-type p53 conformation in Y220C AML but induced limited or no apoptosis unless combined with venetoclax or MDM2/XPO1 inhibition.

intervention_dose: 131I-apamistamab dosimetry-guided therapeutic infusion followed by reduced-intensity conditioning and allo-HCT
indication: Active relapsed/refractory AML, age 55 and over
population_detail: 153 patients randomised (76 apamistamab, 77 conventional care). Active disease at randomisation was required. Prior allogeneic or autologous HSCT was an exclusion, so this patient could not have enrolled.
comparator: Conventional salvage care, with allo-HCT if CR/CRp achieved; crossover permitted
median_dor_or_pfs: Durable CR by definition lasted at least 180 days
safety_summary: Grade 3+ treatment-related events were 59.7% versus 59.2%, essentially identical between arms. 100-day non-relapse mortality was 12.2% versus 14.3% and 1-year NRM 26.1% versus 28.6%; treatment-related deaths were 3 (4.2%) versus 4 (5.3%).

toxicities.notes: grade 2-4 aGVHD in transplanted patients; 35.7% conventional care

notes: The randomised proof that a patient with active leukaemia can be transplanted when conditioning is antigen-targeted; the 0% control arm is what makes the comparison stark. Overall survival did not separate (HR 0.99), which crossover dilutes. Prior HCT was excluded, so this informs mechanism rather than eligibility. Safety from PMC11709001.

exclusion_reason: Preclinical — disseminated murine AML model with syngeneic transplant; no clinical results are published for NCT03670966.
notes: Logged so the thinness is visible: the alpha-emitter conditioning protocol that would accept this patient's prior reduced-intensity allograft has no published human efficacy data at all.

intervention_label: FLAMSA-RIC (sequential fludarabine/cytarabine/amsacrine, reduced-intensity conditioning, prophylactic DLI)
intervention_dose: Fludarabine 30 mg/m2, cytarabine 2 g/m2, amsacrine 100 mg/m2 for 4 days; after 3 days rest, 4 Gy TBI + ATG + cyclophosphamide 80-120 mg/kg; prophylactic DLI from day +120
indication: High-risk AML and MDS, including progressive or refractory disease
population_detail: 75 consecutive patients, median age 52.3. 59 had progressive or refractory disease; unfavourable karyotype in 49% of informative patients; 68 had contraindications to standard conditioning. 31 had HLA-identical sibling donors.
median_dor_or_pfs: 2-year overall survival 42% and leukemia-free survival 40%
safety_summary: The report gives no per-term adverse-event table; outcome was driven by non-relapse mortality and GVHD, with survival best in patients receiving high CD34+ cell doses and having limited GVHD.
notes: Patients with refractory disease and complex cytogenetics did as well as better-prognosis subgroups here, which is the argument for cytoreduce-then-graft without waiting for remission. Cohort was overwhelmingly first transplant, so it understates the risk of a second graft. Checked PubMed abstract and the JCO publisher page; the 2005 paper reports non-relapse mortality and GVHD narratively with no per-term AE table, and the study predates trial registration so there is no ClinicalTrials.gov AE tab.

intervention_label: FLAMSA sequential conditioning in AML in first or second complete remission (EBMT)
exclusion_reason: Wrong disease state — all 265 patients were transplanted in CR1 or CR2, whereas this patient has 85% marrow blasts. The refractory-disease FLAMSA evidence is Schmid 2005.
journal: Biology of Blood and Marrow Transplantation
notes: Read for a larger FLAMSA denominator. The 2-year OS of 56.1% here belongs to remission patients and should not be quoted for active disease.

intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT for haematologic relapse of acute leukemia
intervention_dose: Second allograft from the original or an alternative donor; conditioning at investigator discretion
indication: Acute leukemia relapsing after a first allogeneic HCT
population_detail: 179 second transplants, 75 after a matched related first transplant and 104 after an unrelated first transplant. Remission duration after the first transplant and disease stage at the second were the two prognostic factors carried into multivariate analysis.
outcome: Overall survival at 2 years from the second transplant
median_dor_or_pfs: 2-year OS 39% +/- 7% after a related second transplant and 19% +/- 4% after an unrelated one

outcomes.name: HR_OS
outcomes.notes: short remission duration after first HCT

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: CR after second HCT, independent of donor; half relapsed again

safety_summary: The report is survival-focused and does not tabulate per-term adverse events; failure was driven by second relapse in about half of those achieving CR.
notes: The stratum that fits this patient is the related-donor first transplant group at 37% +/- 6% two-year survival, roughly half again better than the unrelated group. Changing donor for the second graft neither helped nor hurt. Checked PubMed abstract and the JCO page; this is a registry survival analysis with no adverse-event tabulation and no registration record to fall back on.

intervention_label: Second allogeneic transplant for relapse — EBMT registry with remission-duration stratification
intervention_dose: Second allograft, donor and conditioning at centre discretion
indication: Relapse of malignant disease after a first allogeneic transplant
population_detail: 2632 second allogeneic transplants performed for relapse after a first transplant, across diagnoses. Sibling donor was a favourable factor; changing donor was not.
outcome: Relapse-free survival at 5 years after the second transplant
median_dor_or_pfs: 15% remained relapse-free to 5 years after the second transplant

outcomes.name: other
outcomes.notes: longer remission after first transplant, longer inter-transplant interval, low disease burden, younger age, sibling donor and absence of grade II-IV acute or chronic GVHD after the first transplant all predicted better survival

safety_summary: Adverse events are not tabulated in this registry analysis; the outcome measures are survival and relapse.
notes: The largest denominator on second transplants and the source of the stratification this case turns on: a six-year remission and a sibling donor sit on the favourable side of every listed factor except disease burden, which sits badly at 85% blasts. Effect sizes for individual strata are not published as separate survival estimates. Checked PubMed abstract and the Bone Marrow Transplantation page; EBMT registry analyses of this type carry no AE data and there is no registration record.

intervention_label: Salvage of AML relapse after reduced-intensity allogeneic HCT — prognostic score
intervention_dose: Cytoreductive therapy followed by DLI or second allogeneic HCT for consolidation
indication: AML relapsing after reduced-intensity conditioning allogeneic HCT
population_detail: 263 relapsed patients drawn from 2815 RIC transplants performed in CR between 1999 and 2008. Prognostic groups were built from remission duration after HCT, marrow blast percentage and prior acute GVHD.
design: Retrospective registry analysis (EBMT Acute Leukaemia Working Party)
outcome: Overall survival at 2 years from relapse
median_dor_or_pfs: Best prognostic group 32% +/- 7% at 2 years, middle 19% +/- 4%, worst 4% +/- 2%

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: CR reinduced; remission duration after HCT was the only predictor of response

outcomes.name: HR_OS
outcomes.notes: remission after HCT longer than 5 months

outcomes.name: HR_OS
outcomes.notes: absence of acute GVHD after HCT

safety_summary: Survival, response and prognostic grouping are the reported outcomes; no per-term adverse-event data appear in the paper.
notes: This patient splits the score: remission far beyond 5 months puts her in the favourable band, 85% marrow blasts puts her in the unfavourable one. Long-term survival occurred almost only where cytoreduction achieved CR before DLI or a second graft, which is the case for treating the blast burden first. Checked PubMed abstract and the Blood page; the registry analysis reports survival and prognostic grouping only, with no AE table and no registration record.

intervention_label: Donor lymphocyte infusion for first haematologic relapse of AML after allogeneic HCT
intervention_dose: Donor lymphocyte infusion, dose and schedule at centre discretion, with or without preceding cytoreduction
indication: AML in first haematologic relapse after allogeneic HCT
population_detail: 399 patients in first relapse after HCT; 171 received DLI and 228 did not. Risk factors examined within the DLI group included marrow blast burden, karyotype, sex and remission status at infusion.
design: Retrospective registry comparison (EBMT Acute Leukaemia Working Party)
median_dor_or_pfs: 2-year survival 56% +/- 10% when DLI was given in remission or with favourable karyotype; 15% +/- 3% when given in aplasia or with active disease

outcomes.name: OS_rate
outcomes.subgroup: DLI in remission or favourable karyotype

outcomes.name: OS_rate
outcomes.subgroup: DLI in aplasia or with active disease

safety_summary: The analysis reports survival and risk factors rather than a per-term adverse-event table; GVHD after DLI is discussed narratively as the mechanism of both benefit and harm.
notes: Sets the honest ceiling on sibling DLI here. Late relapse is in this patient's favour, but 85% blasts and an adverse karyotype put her in the 15% +/- 3% stratum, not the 56% one, unless cytoreduction gets her into remission first. Checked PubMed abstract and the JCO page; GVHD is discussed as mechanism rather than tabulated, and the registry study has no registration record to query.

intervention_label: DLI versus second allogeneic HCT after debulking therapy
intervention_dose: DLI or second allograft, both after debulking chemotherapy
indication: Acute leukemia relapsing after allogeneic HCT
population_detail: 46 patients (30 AML, 16 ALL), median age 38; 27 received a second allograft and 19 received DLI, all after debulking.
outcome: Overall survival, DLI versus second allogeneic HCT

outcomes.name: OS
outcomes.effect_size: higher with second allo-HCT on univariate analysis
outcomes.notes: difference did not persist on multivariate analysis

outcomes.name: other
outcomes.effect_size: time to relapse was the only significant predictor of OS and DFS

safety_summary: Comparative survival and relapse are the reported outcomes; the paper does not tabulate adverse events by term.
notes: Small (46 patients) and underpowered, so the equivalence claim is weak. Its use is that once debulking is applied to both, remission duration rather than the choice between DLI and a second graft drove outcome. Checked PubMed abstract and the Experimental Hematology page; the retrospective cohort reports survival and relapse only, with no per-term AE table and no registration record.

exclusion_reason: Biomarker mismatch and out of mechanism scope — menin inhibitors act on KMT2A-rearranged or NPM1-mutant leukemia. This patient has KMT2A amplification (4 copies) with no rearrangement and no reported NPM1 mutation, so the drug does not target any nominated feature.
notes: Read specifically to confirm the eligibility biology before dropping the class. The dependency reported is on the menin-KMT2A protein interaction in rearranged disease, not on KMT2A copy number.
